title: Supabase claims-based RBAC: authorize('messages.read') on org roles carried in the JWT
issue: Supabase's RBAC guide keeps roles in JWT claims (custom access token hook) and gates every policy through a plpgsql authorize() function. Called per row it parses the claims and probes role_permissions for every message; claims also go stale until the token is refreshed.
symptom: naive_rls (authorize(permission, org_id) per row) pays a jsonb parse plus an index probe per message, orders of magnitude over the explicit semi-join; best_practice_rls (claims turned into an org array once) is close to the target but depends on claims that lag the database. pg_auth reads live OpenFGA relations: one object per org, permission derived from the role relations.

scale.meaning: number of rows in app.messages. orgs = max(scale/200,100), 4 channels per org, scale/100 noise users (min 100) in 2 orgs each; OpenFGA tuples = one per membership (about 2 x scale/100 + 64), so they grow with users, not messages. At 10x (500000): 2500 orgs, 10000 channels, 500k messages, 5000 users, ~10k tuples; the subjects keep their fixed orgs (few_orgs 61-64, many_orgs 1-60) and so keep ~24 and ~450 readable channels' worth of orgs, with 10x the messages per org.

subjects.name: few_orgs
subjects.note: member of orgs 61-64 with roles member, moderator, admin, guest: reads messages in 3 orgs, channels in 4

subjects.name: many_orgs
subjects.note: member of orgs 1-60 (60 entries in app_metadata.orgs): reads messages in 45 orgs, channels in 60
